thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging db-oncall, SRE on-call, and deployment lead for prod errors affecting write path in us-east-1. Alert: increase in 500s and migrations failing on canary nodes.

olivia: seeing 15% error rate on /v1/generate on canary pool, latency spikes, and DB errors: 'column not found' from app logs. Can someone pick this up?

raj: I can grab it — oncall. Pulling logs now. Which deploy went to canary?

olivia: rolled out revision r-2026-03-15-09:12 to canary (10% traffic). Contains migration 20260315_add_user_index.sql.

maria: confirmed. The migration adds a nullable column and a new index; app reads column without feature flag guard so some canary instances are querying the new column.

db-oncall: looking at pgres master in us-east-1. I see repeated errors: ERROR: column "new_user_flag" does not exist at character 123. Stack trace from app shows query using new_user_flag in WHERE clause.

paul-sre: are migrations applied before traffic? We usually run migration -> rollout. Was this reversed?

olivia: we queued migration via release job but canary rollout started concurrently; looks like race where some canaries hit the new code before migration finished on all DBs.

db-oncall: checks: some migration workers marked completed but others failed due to a lock/wait. There's a long-running transaction holding locks on schema_migrations table from job pid 87321.

raj: can we identify which process is holding the lock?

db-oncall: yes: pid 87321 owner=deploy-batch user=deploy_app query="BEGIN; ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN new_user_flag boolean; ..." started 00:18:34 ago. It appears stuck at ALTER INDEX because index creation waiting due to concurrent DDL and an open tx.

maria: that's bad — app instances without column are hitting queries referencing it. Customer impact: small percentage of requests from canary return 500, errors show up in a handful of customers. No broad outage yet.

kate-pm: alert CS and list affected customers. Low to medium impact for a subset of users.

cs-bot: Notifying CS on-call list and creating incident ticket INC-2026-0315-01.

olivia: immediate mitigation option 1: hit the release kill-switch (feature flag) to prevent canary instances from executing code that references new_user_flag. Option 2: rollback canary to previous revision. Option 3: kill the stuck migration transaction and rerun migration properly. Thoughts?

raj: recommend kill-switch + kill stuck tx. Kill switch because it's fastest to stop new errors. Then we can decide to abort migration and re-run in offline window.

db-oncall: to kill tx: I can pg_terminate_backend(87321) but need approval — it will abort the ALTER TABLE in-flight. If we kill it, we must ensure partial changes not left in inconsistent state. The ALTER was not committed.

paul-sre: approved. Do it. We need to coordinate kill-switch first so no new queries expect the column.

olivia: toggling feature flag: /ff toggle new_user_rollout canary false

deploy-bot: Feature flag new_user_rollout set to false for canary segment by olivia.

maria: confirmed that canaries stopped hitting the new code. Error rate dropped from 15% -> 1% in 30s.

db-oncall: running pg_terminate_backend(87321) now.

db-oncall: terminated pid 87321. Confirmed: no active DDL sessions left. Reviewing schema: ALTER TABLE did not complete, column new_user_flag not present.

raj: good. Next steps: schedule a controlled migration window. We must apply migration on a maintenance node, validate, then progressively roll canary again behind flag. Also consider converting to ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS and backward-compatible queries.

maria: agreed — app should use feature flag guard and handle missing column gracefully. We'll open PR to make migration idempotent and code tolerant.

olivia: for immediate: I'm going to halt canary rollout and advance rollback to previous revision r-2026-03-15-08:45. Initiating rollback.

deploy-bot: Rolling back canary traffic to r-2026-03-15-08:45 per olivia.

paul-sre: monitoring for lingering locks or replication lag. Check for blocked queries:

paul-sre: ```sql
SELECT pid, state, wait_event_type, query_start, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle' ORDER BY query_start DESC LIMIT 20;
```

db-oncall: ran check — no blocked DDL or long-running transactions. replication lag normal.

kate-pm: CS notified affected customers with a brief summary and ETA for postmortem.

cs-bot: Customer advisory posted to #customers-affected channel and ticket updated.

raj: assigning follow-ups: DB oncall will co-ordinate a controlled migration window, eng will add guards and make migration idempotent, SRE will update runbook for deploy gating to ensure migration completed before traffic shift.

maria: I'll own the PR for guard + migration fix. Expected PR by EOD.

db-oncall: I'll schedule a maintenance window tomorrow 02:00 UTC to run migration with monitored rollouts; will run ALTER TABLE in a separate non-transactional chunk where possible, create index concurrently, and validate.

olivia: postmortem owner? I can draft initial timeline. Tagging paul-sre for SLO/metrics analysis.

paul-sre: I'll pull graphs for error rate, p50/p95 latency, and replication lag. Also add a note to runbook: do not start canary traffic until migrations return success status from migration job.

maria: action items added to INC-2026-0315-01.

olivia: marking incident as mitigated. Will keep channel open for follow-ups. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-01 marked mitigated by olivia at 2865432580.
